questions.question:

The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The company decided / to phase up its / outdated technology / and embrace innovation.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

__
 
• The phrase **"to phase up its"** is grammatically incorrect. The correct expression is "to phase out its" when referring to discontinuing or replacing something.
 
• **"Phase out"** means to gradually stop using or replace something, which is the intended meaning in this context.
 
• **"Phase up"** is not a standard phrase in English and does not convey the intended meaning of discontinuing outdated technology.
 
• Thus, the error is located in **part 4** of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The company decided to phase out its outdated technology and embrace innovation."*

• **Option 1: "and embrace innovation." **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 2: "The company decided" **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
 
• **Option 3: "outdated technology" **– This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.

questions.question:
Select the most appropriate adjective to fill in the blank.

After coming from a long journey he said, "It feels so _______ to be home".
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '**good**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The adjective "good" is appropriate because it is used to describe how the speaker feels after a long journey, expressing a general sense of well-being.
 
• "Better" is a comparative adjective, which implies a comparison, but there is no comparison being made here.
 
• "Much good" is incorrect because "much" is not typically used before an adjective like "good" in this context.
 
• "Best" is a superlative adjective, which suggests the highest quality, but the sentence does not require a comparison of quality, making it incorrect here.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

**Complete Sentence:** *"After coming from a long journey he said, 'It feels so **good**__ to be home.'*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "better" **– This is a comparative adjective and would imply the speaker is comparing how they feel now with how they felt at some other time, which is not the case here.
 
• **Option 3: "much good" **– "Much" is unnecessary and incorrect in this construction.
 
• **Option 4: "best" **– A superlative adjective is not needed here because the speaker is not comparing the feeling with any other feeling.

questions.question:

A word, number, or other figure that looks the same when viewed (or rotated) upside down.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Ambigram**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"Ambigram"** refers to a word, number, or other figure that looks the same when viewed upside down or rotated. (एम्बिग्राम)

 
 
• **Example:** The word "WOW" is an ambigram because it looks the same when flipped upside down.
 
 
 
• **"Ambigram"** is unique because it retains its symmetry or identical representation regardless of orientation, making it visually appealing in design and art. (एम्बिग्राम)
 
 
• **Example:** Many logos use ambigrams to create designs that can be understood from multiple perspectives.
 
 
 
• Hence, we conclude that the correct word for the given group of words is **"Ambigram."**

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Ambigram**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Anadiplosis** (अनादिप्लोसिस): A rhetorical device where the last word of a clause or sentence is repeated as the first word of the next clause or sentence.

 
 
• **Example:** "Strength through unity, unity through strength."
 
 
 
• **Alliteration** (अनुप्रास): The repetition of the same sound or letter at the beginning of closely connected words.
 
 
• **Example:** "Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers."
 
 
 
• **Anagram** (अक्षर परिवर्तन): A word or phrase formed by rearranging the letters of another word or phrase.
 
 
• **Example:** "Listen" can be rearranged to form "Silent."

options.text: The hard disc of a computer on a desk needs to be repaired at the earliest.

questions.solution:
**The correct answer is option 3.**

**To answer this question, let's break down each sentence to identify the grammatically and contextually correct ones:**

__
 
• **Option 1: "The hard disc of a computer on a desk needs to be repaired at the earliest."**

 
 
• This sentence is incorrect because it uses "a computer" and "a desk," which are both indefinite articles. It suggests that the computer and desk are being referred to as general items, which may not be the case here.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: "A hard disc of the computer on the desk needs to be repaired at the earliest."**
 
 
• This sentence is incorrect because "A hard disc" should be "The hard disc" to refer specifically to the disc of a particular computer already mentioned.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: "The hard disc of the computer on the desk needs to be repaired at the earliest."**
 
 
• This sentence is correct because "The hard disc" refers to a specific disc (the one belonging to the computer on the desk), and the use of "the" clarifies that we are speaking about a specific item.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: "The hard disc of a computer on the desk needs to be repaired at an earliest."**
 
 
• This sentence is incorrect because the phrase "at an earliest" is grammatically wrong. The correct expression is simply "at the earliest," without the indefinite article "an."
 
 

**Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 3."**

**Complete Sentence:** *"The hard disc of the computer on the desk needs to be repaired at the earliest."*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Option 2: "A hard disc of the computer on the desk" **– This part is incorrect because "A" should be "The" to refer to a specific disc.
 
• **Option 4: "at an earliest" **– This is grammatically incorrect; the correct phrase is "at the earliest."
